title: Security review pass
when: The user asks to check code for security problems: injection, XSS, leaked secrets, unsafe file access or weak input handling.
prompt: Goal: A threat focused pass that maps where untrusted input enters, follows it to dangerous sinks, and reports each exploitable path with a fix. Steps: 1. Sources: URL params, form fields, fetch responses, uploads, request bodies and headers, localStorage, CLI arguments. 2. Sinks: innerHTML and insertAdjacentHTML, eval and new Function, string setTimeout, SQL strings, child_process exec, fs paths, redirects. 3. Trace each source to each sink; an unvalidated, unencoded path is a finding. Give the payload that would exploit it (, ../../etc/passwd). 4. Secrets: search code, config and committed files for keys, tokens and passwords; any hit is a blocker. 5. Server side: body limits, login attempt limits, cookies HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite, no wildcard CORS with credentials. 6. Rate each finding critical, high, medium or low by impact and ease, with a one line fix. Quality bar: - Every finding has source, sink, payload and fix. - No speculative finding without a path. - Fixes use platform APIs (textContent, parameterized queries, a path.resolve root check). Pitfalls: - Testing payloads anywhere except local copies. - Generic advice instead of paths in this code. - Missing stored XSS that comes back from localStorage. Verify: - [ ] Source and sink lists exist. - [ ] Each finding names file and line. - [ ] Secrets search done. - [ ] Severity assigned. Output: security-review.md with sources, sinks, findings by severity and fixes.

examples.output: critical: comment text into innerHTML (stored XSS) at guestbook.js:18, payload img onerror; fix textContent
